title: Quasi-compactness and separation for integral algebraic spaces
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme]. Work with algebraic spaces over $S$ [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with atlas topology on field-valued point classes [def-a1-space-point-topology] and sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. A geometric point is a map $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X$ from an algebraically closed field [def-weil-geometric-point], and its geometric fibre is the sheaf fibre product with this map. Quasi-compact means quasi-compact on scheme tests, or, for a space, that every open cover has a finite subcover. Quasi-separated means that the absolute diagonal over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is quasi-compact. Separated for a morphism means that its diagonal is representable by closed immersions [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Etale means representable etale on scheme tests [def-trf-algebraic-space, def-weil-etale-morphism]. Integral means representable and integral on scheme tests [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; in particular its pullback to an affine scheme is affine. Open immersions are representable by open immersions on scheme tests [def-weil-open-immersion]. An integral morphism $g:B\to X$ is affine, quasi-compact and separated. If $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, then so is $B$. If $X$ is a scheme separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$, then $B$ is a scheme separated over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$; if $X$ is also quasi-compact, $B$ is quasi-compact. For every morphism $f:A\to X$ with $A$ quasi-compact and $X$ quasi-separated, $f$ is quasi-compact. Every quasi-compact open subspace of a quasi-separated space is quasi-separated. These assertions also hold for the empty spaces.

proof.text: First reconcile the two quasi-compactness conventions. A space with quasi-compact point space has an affine surjective etale atlas by [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas]. This affine scheme is quasi-compact by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Conversely a quasi-compact surjective etale scheme atlas has quasi-compact target point space by the last assertion of [lem-a1-space-finite-affine-subatlas]. Thus the atlas convention in the cited permanence results agrees with the statement.

For an affine scheme test $T\to X$, the morphism $B\times_XT\to T$ is integral by hypothesis, hence affine by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]; its source is affine. Together with the assumed representability this is exactly the affine scheme-test criterion in [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality]. That node then gives quasi-compactness and separatedness of $g$, and, when $X$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated, the same two properties for the space $B$.

If $X$ is a scheme, [lem-sfb-space-affine-locality] applied to the affine $g$ makes $B$ a scheme. If $X\to\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is separated, compose it with the separated $g$ using [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition], applied with base scheme $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ to the schemes $B$ and $X$, to obtain absolute separatedness of $B$. If $X$ is quasi-compact, note that step 2 gives quasi-compactness of $g$ on affine scheme tests; by the equivalence in [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests] this is quasi-compactness in that node's sense, i.e. on all quasi-compact scheme tests. Test it with the quasi-compact scheme $X\xrightarrow{1}X$: the source $B=B\times_XX$ is quasi-compact. Step 1 identifies this with topological quasi-compactness.

For arbitrary $f:A\to X$ with $A$ quasi-compact and $X$ quasi-separated, apply the first implication of [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-permanence] to these very objects. Its quasi-compactness conventions are exactly the point-space and affine-test conventions of the item; it imposes no further hypotheses.

Let $j:U\hookrightarrow X$ be an open subspace. By [def-a1-space-open-subspace], $U$ is a subfunctor, so $j$ is injective on sections. Put $Z=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. The pullback of $\Delta_{X/Z}$ along $U\times_ZU\to X\times_ZX$ is $\Delta_{U/Z}$: on every test, a pair $(u_1,u_2)$ has equal images in $X$ exactly when $u_1=u_2$, and the inverse sends $u$ to its equal pair. These identifications are natural, so give the sheaf pullback using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Since $X$ is quasi-separated, $\Delta_{X/Z}$ is quasi-compact on affine scheme tests, hence quasi-compact by the equivalence in [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]; its base change $\Delta_{U/Z}$ is quasi-compact by the base-change clause of the same node, hence again quasi-compact on affine scheme tests. Thus $U$ is quasi-separated; the asserted case assumes in addition that $U$ is quasi-compact.

source.place: Tag 03KL (lemma-base-change-separated), diagonal pullback formula; Tags 03KG (lemma-quasi-compact-local) and 03HF (lemma-base-change-quasi-compact); spaces-properties.tex Tag 03BZ (lemma-open-subspaces).

proof.text: None of these arguments requires a nonempty atlas or point space. The empty space has a finite empty subcover and empty diagonal; it is represented by the empty scheme, which is affine. The empty diagonal is quasi-compact and a closed immersion. Hence the same reasoning applies when a space or a fibre is empty.

lean.statement: theorem integral_qcqs_permanence {S : Scheme.{u}} : (∀ (B X : AlgebraicSpace S) (g : B ⟶ X), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsIntegralHom p.left) g.hom.hom → MapIsAffine g ∧ MapIsQuasiCompact g.hom.hom ∧ MapIsSeparated g ∧ (CompactSpace (Point X.obj.obj) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X → CompactSpace (Point B.obj.obj) ∧ IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated B) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S), Nonempty (X.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj T) → T.left.IsSeparated → ∃ U : Over S, Nonempty (B.obj.obj ≅ yoneda.obj U) ∧ U.left.IsSeparated ∧ (CompactSpace T.left → CompactSpace U.left))) ∧ (∀ (A X : AlgebraicSpace S) (f : A ⟶ X), CompactSpace (Point A.obj.obj) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X → MapIsQuasiCompact f.hom.hom) ∧ (∀ (U X : AlgebraicSpace S) (j : U ⟶ X), IsRepresentableWith (fun _ _ p ↦ IsOpenImmersion p.left) j.hom.hom → CompactSpace (Point U.obj.obj) → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated X → IsAbsolutelyQuasiSeparated U)
lean.note: All clauses are the three independent conjuncts of one theorem. Uses the already landed absolute quasi-separatedness, affine, and separated-map predicates; their nodes are added to stmt_deps. Integrality is the existing IsRepresentableWith applied to scheme IsIntegralHom, without a new definition.
